title: The Secret Code of Every Number
body: Imagine you are a master locksmith. Every number in the universe is a lock, and prime numbers are the only keys. Here is the magical truth: **every whole number greater than 1 can be unlocked using a unique combination of prime number keys — and this combination is always the same, no matter how you try to unlock it!** This is the secret that ancient mathematicians discovered thousands of years ago. In this chapter, you will learn Euclid's powerful tools, the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, and how to prove that some numbers — like √2 — can never be written as a fraction. Get ready to think like a mathematician!
body_hi: कल्पना करो कि तुम एक महान ताला बनाने वाले हो। ब्रह्मांड की हर संख्या एक ताला है, और अभाज्य संख्याएँ (Prime Numbers) ही एकमात्र चाबियाँ हैं। यह जादुई सत्य है: **1 से बड़ी हर पूर्ण संख्या को अभाज्य संख्याओं की एक अनूठी मेल से खोला जा सकता है — और यह मेल हमेशा एक जैसी होती है!** यही वह रहस्य है जो प्राचीन गणितज्ञों ने हजारों साल पहले खोजा था। इस अध्याय में, तुम यूक्लिड के शक्तिशाली नियम, अंकगणित का मूल प्रमेय, और यह साबित करना सीखोगे कि कुछ संख्याएँ — जैसे √2 — कभी भी एक भिन्न के रूप में नहीं लिखी जा सकतीं।

title: Euclid's Division Lemma
body:
**Euclid's Division Lemma** states: For any two positive integers a and b, there exist **unique** integers q (quotient) and r (remainder) such that:

a = bq + r,    0 ≤ r < b

**Example:** For a = 17 and b = 5:
17 = 5 × 3 + 2, so q = 3, r = 2.

**Key Points:**
- The remainder r is always ≥ 0 and < b
- If r = 0, then b divides a exactly (i.e., b is a factor of a)
- This is NOT just a formula — it guarantees a **unique** solution always exists
- This lemma is the foundation of the **Euclidean Algorithm** for finding HCF
body_hi:
**यूक्लिड का विभाजन सहप्रमेय** कहता है: किन्हीं दो धनात्मक पूर्णांकों a और b के लिए, **अद्वितीय** पूर्णांक q (भागफल) और r (शेषफल) मौजूद होते हैं जो इस समीकरण को पूरा करते हैं:

a = bq + r,    0 ≤ r < b

**उदाहरण:** a = 17 और b = 5 के लिए:
17 = 5 × 3 + 2, इसलिए q = 3, r = 2।

**मुख्य बातें:**
- शेषफल r हमेशा ≥ 0 और < b होता है
- अगर r = 0 हो, तो b, a को पूरी तरह विभाजित करता है
- यह सिर्फ एक सूत्र नहीं है — यह गारंटी देता है कि हल हमेशा **अद्वितीय** होगा
- यह सहप्रमेय HCF निकालने वाले **यूक्लिड एल्गोरिथ्म** की नींव है
body_gu:
**યુક્લિડનો વિભાજન સહ-પ્રમેય** કહે છે: કોઈ પણ બે ધન પૂર્ણાંકો a અને b માટે, **અનન્ય** પૂર્ણાંકો q (ભાગ) અને r (શેષ) અસ્તિત્વ ધરાવે છે:

a = bq + r,    0 ≤ r < b

**ઉદાહરણ:** a = 17 અને b = 5 માટે:
17 = 5 × 3 + 2, એટલે q = 3, r = 2.

**મુખ્ય મુદ્દા:**
- શેષ r હંમેશાં ≥ 0 અને < b હોય
- જો r = 0 હોય, તો b, a ને સંપૂર્ણ ભાગ આપે
- આ ફક્ત સૂત્ર નથી — ઉકેલ **અનન્ય** હોય છે
- આ **HCF** શોધવાના Euclidean Algorithm નો આધાર છે

title: The Juice Box Analogy
body: Tell students: 'Think of Euclid's Division Lemma like packing juice boxes. If you have a juice boxes and each carton holds b boxes, you fill q full cartons with exactly r boxes left over. The remainder r must always be **less than b** — if it were b or more, you could pack one more carton!' This makes the constraint 0 ≤ r < b feel completely natural.
body_hi: छात्रों से कहो: 'यूक्लिड के सहप्रमेय को जूस बॉक्स पैक करने जैसा समझो। अगर a जूस बॉक्स हैं और हर डिब्बे में b बॉक्स आते हैं, तो q पूरे डिब्बे भरते हो और r बॉक्स बचते हैं। शेषफल r हमेशा **b से कम** होना चाहिए — अगर b या उससे ज़्यादा होता, तो एक और डिब्बा भर सकते थे!'
body_gu: વિદ્યાર્થીઓને કહો: 'યુક્લિડના સહ-પ્રમેયને જ્યૂસ બૉક્સ ભરવા જેવો વિચારો. a જ્યૂસ બૉક્સ છે અને દરેક કાર્ટનમાં b બૉક્સ આવે, તો q પૂર્ણ કાર્ટન ભરાય અને r બૉક્સ વધે. શેષ r **b કરતાં ઓછો** જ હોઈ શકે — b કે વધુ હોય તો વધુ એક કાર્ટન ભરી શકાત!'

question: Exercise 1.1, Q2: Show that any positive odd integer is of the form 6q+1, 6q+3, or 6q+5, where q is some integer.
question_hi: अभ्यास 1.1, प्र.2: दर्शाओ कि कोई भी धनात्मक विषम पूर्णांक 6q+1, 6q+3, या 6q+5 के रूप में होता है, जहाँ q कोई पूर्णांक है।
question_gu: કસરત 1.1, પ્ર.2: બતાવો કે કોઈ પણ ધન વિષમ (odd) પૂર્ણાંક 6q+1, 6q+3 અથવા 6q+5 સ્વરૂપ ધરાવે છે.
solution:
Let a be any positive integer. By Euclid's lemma with b=6:
a = 6q + r, where r \in \0,1,2,3,4,5\).

- r=0: a=6q → even
- r=1: a=6q+1 → **odd** ✓
- r=2: a=6q+2 → even
- r=3: a=6q+3 → **odd** ✓
- r=4: a=6q+4 → even
- r=5: a=6q+5 → **odd** ✓

Since a is odd, it must be of the form 6q+1, 6q+3, or 6q+5. ∎

question: Exercise 1.1, Q4: Use Euclid's lemma to show that the square of any positive integer is either of the form 3m or 3m+1 for some integer m.
question_hi: अभ्यास 1.1, प्र.4: यूक्लिड के सहप्रमेय का उपयोग करके दर्शाओ कि किसी भी धनात्मक पूर्णांक का वर्ग 3m या 3m+1 रूप में होता है।
question_gu: કસરત 1.1, પ્ર.4: Euclid's lemma વડે બતાવો કે ધન પૂર્ણાંકનો વર્ગ 3m અથવા 3m+1 સ્વરૂપ ધરાવે છે.
solution:
Let a be a positive integer. By b=3: a = 3q, 3q+1, or 3q+2.

**Case 1:** a=3q → a² = 9q² = 3(3q²) = 3m ✓
**Case 2:** a=3q+1 → a² = 9q²+6q+1 = 3(3q²+2q)+1 = 3m+1 ✓
**Case 3:** a=3q+2 → a² = 9q²+12q+4 = 9q²+12q+3+1 = 3(3q²+4q+1)+1 = 3m+1 ✓

So a² is always of the form 3m or 3m+1. ∎

question: Exercise 1.1, Q5: Use Euclid's lemma to show that the cube of any positive integer is of the form 9m, 9m+1, or 9m+8.
question_hi: अभ्यास 1.1, प्र.5: यूक्लिड के सहप्रमेय से दर्शाओ कि किसी भी धनात्मक पूर्णांक का घन 9m, 9m+1, या 9m+8 रूप में होता है।
question_gu: કસરત 1.1, પ્ર.5: ધન પૂર્ણાંકનો ઘન 9m, 9m+1 અથવા 9m+8 સ્વરૂપ ધરાવે છે — Euclid's lemma વડે બતાવો.
solution:
By b=3: a = 3q, 3q+1, 3q+2.

**Case 1:** (3q)³ = 27q³ = 9(3q³) = 9m ✓
**Case 2:** (3q+1)³ = 27q³+27q²+9q+1 = 9(3q³+3q²+q)+1 = 9m+1 ✓
**Case 3:** (3q+2)³ = 27q³+54q²+36q+8 = 9(3q³+6q²+4q)+8 = 9m+8 ✓

Hence cube of any positive integer is of form 9m, 9m+1, or 9m+8. ∎

title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (FTA)
body:
**Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic:** Every composite number can be expressed (factorized) as a product of primes, and this factorization is **unique**, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.

In other words: Every integer n > 1 has a unique prime factorization:
n = p₁^a₁) × p₂^a₂) × ... × pk^ak)

**Examples:**
- 12 = 2² × 3 (unique!)
- 140 = 2² × 5 × 7 (unique!)
- 3825 = 3² × 5² × 17 (unique!)

**Using FTA for HCF and LCM:**
- **HCF** = Product of the **smallest powers** of common prime factors
- **LCM** = Product of the **greatest powers** of all prime factors
- Key relation: **HCF × LCM = Product of the two numbers**

n = p₁^a₁) × p₂^a₂) × ... × pk^ak)

**उदाहरण:** 12 = 2² × 3; 140 = 2² × 5 × 7; 3825 = 3² × 5² × 17

**HCF और LCM:**
- **HCF** = साझा अभाज्य गुणनखंडों की **सबसे छोटी घातों** का गुणनफल

- **HCF × LCM = दोनों संख्याओं का गुणनफल**

title: Factor Tree Technique
body: Draw a factor tree! Start with the number at the top, branch into any two factors, keep branching until all leaves are prime. Circle all the leaves — those are your prime factors. For HCF: take only factors that appear in ALL trees, using the smallest power. For LCM: take ALL factors from ALL trees, using the largest power.

For 6ⁿ to end in 0, it must be divisible by 10 = 2 × 5.

title: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
title_hi: अपरिमेय संख्याएँ और विरोधाभास द्वारा प्रमाण
body:
**Irrational numbers** cannot be written in the form p/q where p, q are integers and q ≠ 0. Their decimal expansion is **non-terminating and non-recurring** (e.g., √2 = 1.41421356...)

**Proof that √2 is irrational:**
Assume √2 = r/s, where r, s are coprime integers (HCF=1), s≠0.

**Step 1:** Squaring: 2 = r²/s² → r² = 2s²

**Step 2:** So 2 divides r². By theorem (if prime p|a², then p|a), 2 divides r.

**Step 3:** Write r = 2c. Then (2c)² = 2s² → 4c² = 2s² → s² = 2c²

**Step 4:** So 2 divides s² → 2 divides s.

**Step 5:** Both r and s are divisible by 2 — this **contradicts** HCF(r,s) = 1!

**Conclusion:** Our assumption was wrong. √2 is **irrational**. ∎

This same method proves √3, √5, √7, and many more are irrational.
body_hi:
**अपरिमेय संख्याएँ** p/q रूप में नहीं लिखी जा सकतीं। उनका दशमलव विस्तार **अनवसानी और अनावर्ती** होता है (जैसे √2 = 1.41421356...)

**√2 के अपरिमेय होने का प्रमाण:**
मान लो √2 = r/s (जहाँ r,s सहभाज्य, HCF=1, s≠0)

**चरण 1:** वर्ग करो: r² = 2s² → 2, r को विभाजित करता है → r = 2c

**चरण 2:** (2c)² = 2s² → s² = 2c² → 2, s को भी विभाजित करता है

**चरण 3:** r और s दोनों सम हैं — यह HCF=1 से **विरोधाभास** है!

**निष्कर्ष:** हमारी मान्यता गलत थी। √2 **अपरिमेय** है। ∎
body_gu:
**અપ્રમેય (Irrational)** = p/q સ્વરૂપ ના હોય. decimal → non-terminating, non-recurring.

**√2 અપ્રમેય છે — પ્રમાણ:**
ધારો √2=r/s (HCF=1). → r²=2s² → 2|r → r=2c → s²=2c² → 2|s → r,s બંનેના 2 ગુણક → HCF≠1 **વિરોધ!** → √2 અપ્રમેય ∎

question:
Exercise 1.3, Q3: Prove that the following are irrational:
(i) 2+√3
(ii) 5 - √3
(iii) 1/(2-√3)
solution:
**(i)** Assume 2+√3 = a/b → √3 = a/b - 2 = (a-2b)/b → rational → Contradiction ∎

**(ii)** Assume 5-√3 = a/b → √3 = 5 - a/b = (5b-a)/b → rational → Contradiction ∎

**(iii)** Rationalize: 1/(2-√3) = (2+√3)/((2-√3)(2+√3)) = (2+√3)/(4-3) = 2+√3
Since 2+√3 is irrational (proved in i), 1/(2-√3) is **irrational**. ∎

title: Decimal Expansions of Rational Numbers
body:
**Theorem 1:** Let x = p/q be a rational number in simplest form. If the prime factorization of q is of the form **2ⁿ × 5ᵐ** (where n, m ≥ 0), then x has a **terminating** decimal expansion.

**Theorem 2:** If the prime factorization of q is **NOT** of the form 2ⁿ × 5ᵐ (i.e., it contains other prime factors like 3, 7, 11, ...), then x has a **non-terminating repeating (recurring)** decimal expansion.

**Examples:**
| Fraction | Denominator | Factorization | Type |
|----------|-------------|---------------|------|
| 3/8 | 8 | 2³ | **Terminating** (= 0.375) |
| 13/3125 | 3125 | 5⁵ | **Terminating** |
| 7/6 | 6 | 2 × 3 | **Non-terminating repeating** |
| 2/11 | 11 | 11 | **Non-terminating repeating** |
| 1/15 | 15 | 3 × 5 | **Non-terminating repeating** |

**Key Insight:** To convert a terminating decimal, multiply numerator and denominator to make the denominator a power of 10.

Example: 13/3125 = 13/5⁵ = (13 × 2⁵)/(5⁵ × 2⁵) = 416/100000 = 0.00416
body_hi:
**प्रमेय 1:** यदि q का अभाज्य गुणनखंड **2ⁿ × 5ᵐ** रूप में हो, तो p/q का **सांत दशमलव विस्तार** होगा।

**प्रमेय 2:** यदि q में 2 और 5 के अलावा भी अभाज्य गुणनखंड हों, तो p/q का **असांत आवर्ती दशमलव विस्तार** होगा।

**उदाहरण:**
- 3/8 = 0.375 → **सांत** (8 = 2³)
- 7/6 → **असांत आवर्ती** (6 = 2 × 3)
- 1/15 → **असांत आवर्ती** (15 = 3 × 5)
body_gu:
**Theorem 1:** q=2ⁿ×5ᵐ → **Terminating**
**Theorem 2:** q ≠ 2ⁿ×5ᵐ → **Non-terminating recurring**

ઉdaheran:
- 3/8 → terminating (0.375)
- 7/6 → non-terminating recurring
- 1/15 → non-terminating recurring

title: The 'Look at Denominator Only' Shortcut
body: Exam shortcut: Simplify the fraction first. Then look ONLY at the denominator. If ALL its prime factors are from {2, 5} only → terminating. If ANY other prime (3, 7, 11, 13...) appears → non-terminating repeating. You do NOT need to actually divide!

title: Common Mistakes — Real Numbers
body:
**Mistake 1:** Using HCF × LCM = a × b for three numbers. ❌
→ This formula works ONLY for TWO numbers.

**Mistake 2:** Forgetting to simplify before checking decimal type. ❌
→ Always simplify 6/15 to 2/5 first!

**Mistake 3:** Starting proof by contradiction without saying 'Let r and s be coprime.' ❌
→ Always state HCF(r,s)=1 at the beginning.

**Mistake 4:** Saying LCM is always larger than HCF. ❌
→ LCM = HCF when both numbers are equal (e.g., HCF(5,5)=LCM(5,5)=5).

**Mistake 5:** Confusing terminating with non-recurring. ❌
→ Terminating = stops. Non-terminating recurring = goes on with repeating block. Non-terminating non-recurring = irrational!

title: Chapter Summary: Real Numbers
body:
**What We Learned:**

🔷 **Euclid's Division Lemma:** a = bq + r (0 ≤ r < b) — basis for finding HCF step by step.

🔷 **Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic:** Every composite number has a **unique** prime factorization.

🔷 **HCF by FTA:** Smallest powers of common prime factors.

🔷 **LCM by FTA:** Greatest powers of all prime factors.

🔷 **Key Formula:** HCF × LCM = a × b (for two numbers).
